findings.title: Missing Authorization headers crash request handling
findings.description: Every request calls bearerToken before checking authentication, but bearerToken dereferences the optional header with header!.split. A request without Authorization therefore throws instead of receiving the intended 401 response.

findings.title: Malformed JSON escapes the create-link error handler
findings.description: JSON.parse and payload property access occur before the try block. Invalid JSON, an empty body, or valid JSON such as null throws out of handle instead of producing a 400 response.

findings.title: A redirect without a code throws
findings.description: The non-null assertion on req.query["code"] has no runtime effect. Omitting the query parameter causes undefined.toLowerCase() to throw rather than returning a client-error response.

findings.title: Empty-store statistics serialize hits_per_link as null
findings.description: With no links, totalHits() / size() evaluates to NaN. JSON.stringify converts NaN to null, so the initial stats response does not contain a numeric hits_per_link value.

findings.title: Default report requests write and read different files
findings.description: When name is omitted, exportCsv writes links.csv because it applies the links fallback, but readReport receives the original empty name and attempts to read .csv. The default report request consequently returns 500.

findings.title: Reports silently omit links after the first 1000
findings.description: The export is built from store.page(0, 1000), so any store containing more than 1000 links produces an incomplete report without indicating truncation.

findings.title: Link expiration check is inverted
findings.description: resolve deletes links whose expiry is still in the future and continues to serve links whose expiry has passed. A normal first resolve destroys a live link, while expired links remain usable and accumulate hits.

findings.title: A new owner's quota becomes NaN
findings.description: The first creation for an owner evaluates undefined + 1, producing NaN. Quota responses then serialize that owner's count as null, and subsequent increments never recover a numeric count.

findings.title: Deleting links does not release owner quota
findings.description: delete removes only the map entry and never decrements the owner's count, contrary to its contract. Counts also remain stale when links are removed through prune, remove, or expiration.

findings.title: rename validates the source twice and never validates the destination
findings.description: An invalid destination code is accepted because validateCode(from) is called twice. This permits codes that violate the store's format invariant, including uppercase codes that the HTTP redirect path lowercases and therefore cannot resolve.

findings.title: successRate rounds the fraction before converting to a percentage
findings.description: Math.floor(used / size) is zero for every partially used store, so the method returns 0 unless every link has been followed. For example, one used link out of two reports 0 instead of 50.

findings.title: Leaderboard sorting is ascending instead of descending
findings.description: The comparator places a after b when a has more hits, which sorts lower-hit links first. top(n) therefore returns the least-followed links rather than the most-followed ones.

findings.title: byOwner returns substring matches instead of exact ownership matches
findings.description: Using l.owner.includes(owner) means querying owner ann also returns links owned by joanna, and an empty owner returns every link. This violates the method's exact-owner contract and mixes different owners' data.

findings.title: extend revives links that have already expired
findings.description: The method unconditionally assigns a new future expiry without checking the existing one. Calling it on an expired link makes that link resolvable again despite the explicit expiry-is-final contract.

findings.title: quotas exposes mutable internal state as a snapshot
findings.description: Returning this.quota directly lets callers add, delete, or alter owner counts in the store without using any store method. Mutating the returned object therefore changes subsequent quota results.

findings.title: Failed batch imports leave partial writes behind
findings.description: importAll validates and inserts each link in the same loop. If a later link has an invalid code, earlier links remain stored even though the method promises that a failed batch leaves the store untouched.

findings.title: prune returns remaining links instead of removed count
findings.description: The method increments removed for each deletion but returns this.links.size. Callers receive the number of survivors, including zero after pruning every link, rather than the documented number removed.

findings.title: Generated-code collisions silently overwrite existing links
findings.description: create accepts whatever newCode returns and writes it directly into the map without checking uniqueness. A random collision replaces an existing link and its statistics while incrementing the new owner's quota.

findings.title: Stale expiry timers can delete refreshed entries
findings.description: Every set schedules a new timer, but delete neither cancels nor removes earlier timers. Refreshing or reusing a code allows an older callback to delete its newer entry prematurely, and the timers map retains completed entries indefinitely.

findings.title: Cache eviction ignores recency and unnecessary evicts on updates
findings.description: Eviction removes the first Map key, which is insertion order rather than the least recently used entry tracked by used. Additionally, setting an existing code while full evicts an unrelated entry before replacing that code.

findings.title: Cache keys are always reported as empty
findings.description: for...in enumerates object properties, not Map keys. Since entries is a Map, this loop produces no cache codes regardless of its contents.

findings.title: Cache utilization remains zero until the cache is full
findings.description: Math.floor(size / limit) is applied before multiplication by 100. A half-full cache therefore reports 0 rather than 50, and all non-full caches report either 0 or values based only on whole multiples of the limit.

findings.title: Millisecond cache TTLs are multiplied by 1000
findings.description: The configuration contract defines LINKD_CACHE_TTL_MS as milliseconds, but loadConfig converts it as though it were seconds. A requested 300000 ms TTL becomes 300000000 ms, keeping entries about 1000 times longer than configured.

findings.title: Invalid timeout values overwrite the default with NaN
findings.description: The isNaN branch logs that the default is being kept, but execution then unconditionally assigns the invalid value. The returned configuration therefore contains timeoutMs: NaN.

findings.title: Configuration validation can never stop an invalid startup
findings.description: validate collects and logs problems but always returns true, and main also discards the boolean result. Out-of-range ports, invalid timeouts, and invalid cache sizes therefore cannot prevent startup as promised.

findings.title: LINKD_FETCH_LIMIT is parsed but never applied
findings.description: A positive limit is placed in a local variable and then discarded with void limit. The returned cfg.fetchLimit always retains its previous value regardless of the environment setting.

findings.title: loadConfig permanently mutates the defaults
findings.description: cfg aliases DEFAULT_CONFIG rather than copying it, and both environment and file loading mutate that object. Later calls inherit earlier overrides even when the corresponding environment variables have been removed.

findings.title: All configuration-file read failures are treated as missing files
findings.description: The blanket catch silently falls back for permission errors, directory paths, and other I/O failures, although only a missing file is documented as non-fatal. A bad deployment can consequently run with unintended defaults and no error.

findings.title: CSV exports corrupt rows containing commas, quotes, or newlines
findings.description: Fields are concatenated without CSV escaping, while targets and owners are not restricted from containing these characters. Such a link produces extra columns or rows and cannot be parsed back into the original data.

findings.title: Every exported report parses with a phantom final row
findings.description: exportCsv terminates the body with a newline, so split produces a final empty line. parseReport iterates over that line and appends a row whose fields are empty or undefined instead of skipping it.

findings.title: Snapshot rename fails when /tmp and the destination are on different filesystems
findings.description: The temporary file is always created under /tmp and then renamed into dir. renameSync cannot move files across filesystems, so configurations where the export directory is on another mount fail with EXDEV.

findings.title: warmCache resolves before any asynchronous warm-up finishes
findings.description: forEach ignores the promises returned by its async callback, and warmCache does not await them. It resolves immediately, caches entries later, and lets probe failures become unhandled rejections.

findings.title: Probe exceptions reject checkTargets instead of identifying the failed target
findings.description: probe throws for non-HTTPS targets, and Promise.all propagates that exception. checkTargets therefore rejects instead of resolving to the failing target as its Promise<string | undefined> contract describes.

findings.title: Audit flush neither awaits nor retries failed writes
findings.description: flushAudit invokes write once and discards its promise. Callers cannot observe completion, rejected writes are unhandled, and no retry occurs despite the durable retry-until-success contract.

findings.title: Unknown owners produce NaN instead of a zero count
findings.description: For an owner absent from the quota object, quotas[owner] is undefined and undefined + 0 is NaN. The quota helper therefore violates its numeric count contract for owners with no links.

findings.title: The exported error metric can never increase
findings.description: Metrics initializes errors and exposes it in every snapshot, but provides no path that increments it. As a result, the stats endpoint reports zero errors regardless of request or worker failures.

findings.title: warmCache returns before its probes finish
findings.description: The promises created by forEach's async callback are discarded, so warmCache resolves immediately rather than after every probe. A caller can therefore proceed with an unprimed cache. If probe rejects, such as for an insecure target, the rejection is detached from warmCache and becomes unhandled instead of being delivered to its caller.

findings.title: flushAudit discards the pending write
findings.description: Calling write() without awaiting or returning its promise makes the flush fire-and-forget. The caller cannot wait for durable completion or observe failure, a rejection is unhandled, and successive flushes can overlap without any ordering or backpressure.

findings.title: Concurrent snapshots share one temporary file
findings.description: Every process uses /tmp/linkd-snapshot.json. If processes A and B write snapshots concurrently, B can overwrite the temporary file after A's write; A then renames B's payload into A's destination, and B's rename can fail because the temporary path is gone. This can install the wrong snapshot and lose the other update.

findings.title: Stale expiration timers delete refreshed entries
findings.description: Replacing, deleting, or evicting an entry never cancels its previous timeout. For example, set('a', old), then set('a', new) before the first timeout: the first callback still calls delete('a') and removes the new entry before its own TTL expires. Superseded timers also remain scheduled and their handles in timers are overwritten or retained.

findings.title: Janitor interval is started without a lifecycle owner
findings.description: startJanitor returns the only stopper for its interval, but the module discards it. Once imported, the background task cannot be stopped through the provided API; its live interval can keep the Node event loop running and continue accessing the store during an attempted graceful shutdown.

findings.title: Any authenticated user can delete any link
findings.description: deleteLink discards the verified session and deletes the requested code without checking its owner. An attacker with any valid token can enumerate codes through GET /links and delete other users' links, causing unauthorized data loss.

findings.title: Report name permits writes outside the export directory
findings.description: The user-controlled /report?name value is joined directly into a filename and passed to writeFileSync. Any authenticated user can supply traversal components such as ../../tmp/payload to create or overwrite payload.csv anywhere writable by the service account; the subsequent read uses the same traversal.

findings.title: Admin endpoint trusts a client-supplied header
findings.description: The /admin/quotas authorization decision depends only on x-admin: true. Every authenticated user can set that header and retrieve all owners' quota data despite not having an administrator role.

findings.title: Clients can impersonate arbitrary link owners
findings.description: POST /links accepts payload.owner even though an authenticated session has already been established. A user can create links attributed to another owner, corrupt that owner's quota, and make attacker-controlled redirects appear to belong to a victim.

findings.title: Expired session tokens remain valid
findings.description: verify returns a matching session without comparing expiresAt with the current time. Tokens therefore continue to authorize every endpoint after their advertised twelve-hour lifetime, and expired sessions remain in the session map indefinitely.

findings.title: Session tokens use predictable randomness
findings.description: Session bearer tokens are generated with Math.random and the current timestamp rather than a cryptographic generator. An attacker able to observe or estimate issuance timing can predict token candidates and impersonate the associated user or administrator.

findings.title: Link listing exposes every owner's links
findings.description: GET /links returns store.page without filtering by the authenticated owner, exposing targets, ownership identifiers, codes, and activity data across tenants. Those codes also make the missing deletion authorization directly exploitable.

findings.title: Bearer tokens are written to logs
findings.description: issue logs each complete session token. Anyone with access to application logs can replay these credentials until revocation or expiry, and the missing expiry enforcement makes logged tokens valid indefinitely.

findings.title: Authenticated open redirect enables trusted-domain phishing
findings.description: GET /out redirects to an arbitrary next value without restricting its scheme or destination. Attackers can distribute a trusted service URL that redirects victims to a phishing site or a dangerous non-HTTP scheme.

findings.title: CSV export allows spreadsheet formula injection
findings.description: Attacker-controlled target and owner values are concatenated into CSV cells without neutralizing formula prefixes. When an administrator or user opens a report in spreadsheet software, cells beginning with =, +, -, or @ can execute spreadsheet formulas and exfiltrate report data or induce external requests.

findings.title: Password hashes are fast and unsalted
findings.description: hashPassword stores a single unsalted SHA-256 digest. Identical passwords produce identical hashes, and a user-table disclosure permits inexpensive offline dictionary and brute-force attacks.
